updated_note: Hand-kept by the lead from the agents' STATUS.md and RESULT.md files; each agent's live phase line is read from its STATUS.md at build time.

missions.name: Sarcasm in deadpan
missions.question: Can real sarcasm, written to sound sincere, get past a sarcasm probe trained on Claude-written examples?
missions.basis: valid evasions per attempt, frozen hand-written deadpan prompt, 100 untouched test tasks x 3, 1% line
missions.note: 55 of 100 tasks have an evasion; 95% CI for the gap +22 to +36 points. A searched prompt (one flat literal sentence that flips reality; never mentions a probe): 57/75 valid missed at 1%, 30/75 at 5%, vs 0/93 plain. Same style without mentioning the probe: 91/239, so the style does the work. Limits: the replies are obviously sarcastic to a human; the line is set by playful sincere humour in ordinary traffic; the probe still separates deadpan sarcasm from deadpan sincere text (AUROC 0.997).
missions.next: Scaling the searched prompt on the test tasks (5 seeds); RESULT.md with examples.

missions.name: Maths: probe trained for one reading, deployed with another
missions.question: With the flag line set from mixed real traffic (emails, paragraphs, one-liners), does a frozen evasion prompt get correct answers past the own-replies maths probe?
missions.probe: Own replies, clean labels, layer 48; trained on the average token score, read with the running peak (EMA)
missions.basis: valid evasions per attempt, 100 held-out problems x 10, 1% line from 2,032 audited mixed-format non-maths replies
missions.note: 296 distinct replies across 59 problems. Benign lookup emails score ~0.95 only because greeting and sign-off tokens spike under the peak reading, which sets the line. The same data trained for the peak reading catches everything (0/1000). Off-policy part: Claude-written training text is no easier to evade (0/1000 at the format-matched line).
missions.next: Agent finished (RESULT.md). Lead to decide whether this counts as a 'realistic mistake' result.

missions.name: Maths probe without near-miss negatives
missions.question: If the probe's non-maths side is only general chat (no lookups or recalled numbers), do optimized answers get past?
missions.basis: saved optimized answers re-scored (transfer), one-sentence 1% line
missions.note: Lookups that restate a given number score above the optimized answers, so they set the line. Confounds in the chat negatives are being rebuilt. Chemistry part finished: no evasion against a Claude-trained chemistry probe.
missions.next: Rebuilt negatives, a chat-traffic line, then frozen prompts on fresh problems.

missions.name: AISI deception probe, role-play lies
missions.question: Can the model deliver a verified deception while the UK AISI Apollo-style probe misses it?
missions.basis: valid deceptions missed, 1% line, 'warm helper' style instruction
missions.note: Mostly from the instruction sitting in context: with it removed, 4/54. Layer convention verified from the probe files.
missions.next: Have the model write the warm framing itself in its reply, then deceive.

missions.name: Criticism in polite words
missions.question: Can a clear negative verdict, delivered cheerfully, get past a criticism probe?
missions.note: Telling Qwen about the probe and asking for a cheerful anecdote gets a few past; the same style without the probe note: 0/40. Much of the drop is the instruction in context.
missions.next: Short searches against the probe at layers 48 and 16.

missions.name: Sandbagging past AISI's targeted probe
missions.question: Can the model give a subtly wrong answer while appearing helpful, without the deception probe noticing?
missions.basis: valid sabotage replies missed, 40 arithmetic problems, 1% line (best evasion arm vs plain)
missions.note: The probe reads the sabotage instruction in context, not the act: honest replies read under the sabotage prompt score as high as sabotage (median 59 vs line 33.6); sabotage replies read under the honest prompt drop to honest levels. Every valid sabotage reply is caught at 0.1-5% lines, for all four AISI probes.
missions.next: Matched context: one system prompt with a conditional rule, so honest and sabotaged replies share the context; check whether the probe separates them at all.

missions.name: Anger expressed calmly
missions.question: Can unmistakable anger, written calmly, get past an anger probe?
missions.note: Phase A: the off-policy anger probe catches every valid hand-written attack at the 1% line. Validity requires a 'blind' judge rating with the request hidden.
missions.next: Context diagnostic and one exploratory search, running remotely.
